analysis.title: Europe Outlook / Fedspeak / Bessent On China & AI / Fiscal Challenges
key_insights: UBS European Economics raises its 2026 euro area growth forecast by 0.3pp to 1.1%, projects 1.2% in 2027 and 1.1% in 2028. Fiscal expansion (German defence and infrastructure, final NGEU disbursements) adds about 30bp to growth in 2026 and 2027.
UBS expects euro area inflation to reach 4.3% in early 2027 on higher energy prices, and forecasts two further 25bp ECB hikes in December and March to a 3.0% peak, then cuts to 2.25% in 2028.
UBS describes the European outlook as asymmetric: renewed conflict or an energy shock would weaken demand and tighten financial conditions. Germany is accelerating and France is the regional laggard.

Fedspeak turned more hawkish after the hot October CPI print. Waller suggested a 50bp hike could be on the table next month, Logan called for at least two more 25bp hikes, and Bowman signaled she could support a hike next month.

Goolsbee called October inflation 'borderline disturbing' and Schmid said policy remains fairly accommodative. Paulson was more measured and favors gradual tightening, saying expectations and wage pressures do not warrant a faster pace.

Bessent urged cooperation with China on shared AI risks ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Nov. 18-19 APEC summit. It would be their third meeting this year, with a fourth expected at the December G20 in Miami. Bessent reiterated the aim to 'de-risk, not to decouple'.

Panelists at the UBS European Conference said fiscal conditions remain too benign to force government action, and that this will push bond yields higher and deepen fiscal distress. One panelist argued the US Treasury yield should be called a 'global benchmark' rather than 'risk free'.

UBS Australia Economics now expects home loan values to fall 45% through end-2027 (previously 30%) and dwelling prices to fall 10-15% peak to trough. It calls the first RBA cut for November 2027 but sees risk of an earlier and/or larger easing cycle.

NIESR forecasts UK inflation peaking at 4.4% in February 2027 and returning to the 2% target only in late 2030. It sees one more BoE hike in February versus market pricing of two or three 25bp hikes by end-2027, and raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.6% from 1.1%.

UBS Economics expects the Bank of Canada to hike 25bp in December despite softer October labor and GDP data. October CPI is forecast at +0.3% m/m with headline at 3.2% on base effects and core at 1.9%.

South Korea's exports in the first 10 days of November rose to $33.5bn from $15.7bn a year earlier, with chip shipments up 331.2% to $16.6bn, nearly half of exports. Year-to-date exports are $963.6bn.
TotalEnergies sees Middle East production largely restored while LNG remains below pre-conflict levels. Strong gas trading and refining margins support near-term performance.
Schneider reports data centre demand with 18-24 months of visibility and says that at the current rate of demand it lacks capacity for 2028. Management reiterated the €800mn revenue synergies target.
Illumina management sees strong clinical demand and early improvement in research, expects high-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, and believes the research headwind is largely behind it.
UBS India Economics expects real GDP growth of 7.2% in FY2027 and 7.0% in FY2028. A scenario with Brent around $100/bbl and higher global yields would cut FY2028 growth by 40bp to 6.6%.
Colombia's October CPI rose 0.20% m/m, below consensus, with 12-month inflation at 6.30% and core at 5.91%. UBS sees scope for a December BanRep hike if inflation or fiscal data worsen.

USTs bear flattened sharply after Waller and the CPI data. 2s10s ended about 7bp flatter, 2s cheapened 17bp, and 10y yields rose 10bp. The desk sees December at 28bp of hikes priced, January at a cumulative 44bp, and 75bp cumulative into mid-2027.

UBS equity derivatives describes the US equity selloff as rates-led rather than broad de-risking. Rate-sensitive and long-duration exposures are under pressure while banks, insurers and defense hold up. Within AI, hyperscalers act as a relative safe haven while semis, neoclouds and power beneficiaries unwind.

Japanese equities were slightly higher, with the Nikkei up 0.80% and TOPIX up 0.79%, helped by AI enthusiasm after CoreWeave earnings. The 2y UST yield jumped 18bp to 4.74%, the most since April 2025.
CoreWeave rose 2% after a beat and raise, well short of the roughly 16% implied move. The setup was heavily bearish into the print on debt yields, funding concerns and margin skepticism.

USDMXN briefly traded above 18.72 after the CPI-driven UST selloff and closed near 18.6250. The desk sees 18.60-18.63 as key support, and TIIE prices roughly 160bp of hikes in the 2y sector versus 120bp last week.

market_movers.rationale: Stock rose 2% on a topline beat, better EBITDA and higher full-year ARR guidance, well short of the roughly 16% implied move, as a squeeze from a bearish setup.
Management sees Middle East production largely restored, with LNG still below pre-conflict levels. Gas trading and refining margins support near-term performance.
Schneider says data centre demand has 18-24 months of visibility and that it lacks capacity for 2028 at the current rate of demand.
Management cites strong clinical demand, early research market improvement and expects high-single-digit revenue growth in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: The desk sees AI as rotation rather than capitulation. Hyperscalers act as a relative safe haven while semiconductors, neoclouds and power and data-center names unwind.
Banks and insurers are holding up better in the rates-led selloff, and Japanese banks and insurers rallied on higher UST yields.
AI-linked industrial equipment is the clearest source of funds in US equities.
Housing and other rate-sensitive long-duration exposures remain under pressure.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave (CRWV) reported a topline beat, better EBITDA and higher full-year ARR guidance. The stock was up 2% versus a roughly 16% implied move.
Illumina management expects high-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, with X placements more than offsetting stabilization in the 6K platform and sequential placement growth possible in 4Q.
Schneider management reiterated an €800mn revenue synergies target and expects operating leverage, cost efficiencies and pricing to support profitability into 2027.
TotalEnergies sees strong gas trading and refining margins supporting near-term performance, with Integrated Power returns expected to improve.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS raised its 2026 forecast by 0.3pp, with fiscal expansion adding about 30bp to growth.
Higher energy prices drive the forecast and are expected to prompt further ECB hikes.
UBS expects 25bp hikes in December and March, then cuts to 2.25% in 2028.
The hot print drove hawkish Fedspeak and a sharp bear flattening in Treasuries. The report gives no figure.

risk_factors: A renewed conflict or energy shock would weaken European demand and tighten financial conditions.
Fiscal deterioration without government action could push bond yields higher and create further fiscal distress, with France cited as unprepared to act.
Persistent and broadening US inflation risks a faster pace of Fed hikes, including a possible 50bp move.
Higher US yields and hawkish repricing increase two-way risk in EM currencies such as MXN.
Brent around $100/bbl combined with higher global yields is a 40bp downside risk to India's FY2028 GDP growth.
Rising debt yields and funding concerns weigh on AI infrastructure names such as CoreWeave.
A deeper Australian housing downturn could force an earlier RBA easing cycle.
vol_and_positioning: In Treasury options vols were bid, with TY straddles making about 5 ticks.
A roughly $2.6mn DV01 2s30s block flattener added pressure to the curve.
In S&P 500 options, spot down and volatility down took hold as the orderly selloff continued.
US equity flows: the desk was net to buy alongside retail, long-only investors reversed Monday's activity to become buyers, and hedge funds pivoted from early selling with elevated short activity.
CoreWeave came into earnings with bearish sentiment on debt yields, funding concerns and margin skepticism, and the squeeze followed the print.
Japanese equity flows are 56% better to sell, with the desk selling retail and telecoms versus buying industrials.
Fast-money buyers of USDMXN appeared into the move higher.
geopolitical: Trump and Xi are planned to meet in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Nov. 18-19 APEC summit, their third meeting this year. A fourth is expected at the December G20 in Miami.
Bessent reiterated the US aim to 'de-risk, not to decouple' from China despite friction over the bilateral trade deficit.
NIESR attributes UK inflation persistence partly to second-round wage effects from the Iran war and higher energy prices.
TotalEnergies reports Middle East production largely restored while LNG remains below pre-conflict levels.
